In view of the substantial investment in and growth of these New Jersey facilities, the historical uniformity accorded these facilities and those in New York, and the reliance on these exceptions by many parties, some accomodation in our rules is necessary. One alternative would be to describe the physical location of each of these facilities and make a specific regulatory provision for it as is done in the existing rules. This method is cumbersome, however, and does not afford sufficient flexibility to adapt to future changes in location. In our opinion, it is better to recognize the heavy concentration of rail and marine facilities in northern New Jersey in close proximity to New York City and to describe this area along readily identifiable lines. This area will share the limits of the New York, N.Y., commercial zone on shipments having a prior or subsequent movement by rail or water.
